REROUTED FROM PEER (walled by Moonshot's weekly quota at 02:24Z before it started). You are the cross-family verifier for the owner's highest-priority build; budget two subagents.

VERIFY (cross-family, adversarial) helm task/2741 Lane A: burn flags, one fire-danger snapshot per model family. Lane lane/burn-flags-are-one-snapshot-per-family, worktree <HOMEDIR>/dev/akapug/helm-wt/burn-flags-are-one-snapshot-per-family, tip as --ref (nine commits on trunk, one trunk merge, 21 files, +2650/-68). Built by an opus delegated agent from the melded design at <HOMEDIR>/.helm/helm/journal/2026-09-17-burn-flags-design-meld.md (sections 4.1-4.8 and the Lane A build brief there are the contract; the owner's words are on helm task show 2741). Builder's fab on the tip: 32 modules, Ran 2515 OK. You are the outsider; nobody on this chain may verify it. This is the owner's highest-priority build tonight, so the cost of a wrong APPROVE is a fleet that trusts a wrong colour.

WHAT IT CLAIMS: new helm/burnflags.py (families, derive_money, derive_reach, derive_policy, derive_declared, compose, expiry, overall, fold, write_snapshot, cached_flags, family_flag, watch_notice, line, render, cmd_burn, declare); tests/test_burnflags.py (45 methods, arms F1-F6, F9, F10, F15, F17, F18, F20, F22, F24, F25, F26 per the meld's falsifier ledger); proxywatch folds the flags beside its codex budget pass and writes the board key burn_flags only when the one line changes; codexbudget.watch_notice and NOTICE_TAG deleted, ONE announcer in burnflags latched per family on the COLOUR; helm burn verb (why, declare, --until, --json) in cli, docs/VERBS.md, doctor WARN-only rung, /api/flags on web_quota's 120 s cache, quota tab card, ownerchart block, web_roster staleness rebound to proxywatch.UPSTREAM_CACHE_FRESH_S through a guarded import, two registry rows. Fixtures frozen and redacted under tests/fixtures/burnflags (codex pool snapshot, six anthropic usage-history rows including three reauth-needed, the proxywatch upstream block).

THE BUILDER FLAGGED ITS OWN JUDGEMENT CALLS; ATTACK THESE FIRST: (1) a usage-history row older than the staleness bound is treated as UNREAD for both the money and policy axes; that rule is load-bearing (without it the owner's anthropic ORANGE stops reproducing) and it is a judgement, not a meld ruling. (2) A declaration on an UNMEASURED (GREY) family is applied rather than refused. (3) expiry() prefers the headline axis's own instant over the precedence table. (4) The meld's F1 control sentence (40 percent -> ORANGE) contradicts its own threshold table (ORANGE = best readable account >= 80, derived from the ceiling); the builder followed the table and pinned both bands. (5) GREEN is unreachable in production because its third conjunct needs a non-probing abundance reader that does not exist; render and doctor say so. (6) The builder WROTE LIVE STATE from a lane build: ~/.helm/_global/.state/burn-declarations.json seeded with the owner's reading (anthropic ORANGE, codex RED, five YELLOW, expiring 2026-09-19T00:02Z). Check nothing else on the live estate was touched and that a lane test never reads that live path.

COVERAGE, no priority order: every arm must have a must-hit control that would fail if the property were absent (mutate and see red; a green suite proves nothing about the edit); no test reads a live path or calls a vendor (grep for cred_state, windows(), urlopen, the usage endpoint, the live state dir); F18: no email, account id, user id, token or pool filename on ANY surface (snapshot file, board line, render, why, notice body, doctor output); the read path (cached_flags, family_flag) never probes and never blocks; the board write is scalar-only and only on change; the notice fires once per crossing per family and never on a held colour; a
